Measuring Religious Change

Source: R/measuringreligiouschange-package.R
measuringreligiouschange-package.Rd

Tools for projecting religious-composition change using cohort-component demographic models with religious switching, fertility differentials, and migration.

Measuringreligiouschange is a package developed by the Center for Advanced Studies of Population and Religion (CASPAR) for a joint project with the Pew Research Center as part of the Pew-Templeton Global Religious Futures project. The software package can generate religious group population projections at the global, regional and national level resulting from initial age-sex composition of populations, demographic processes (fertility, mortality and migration) and religious processes (transmission of religion between generations and religious switching). The package is a flexible tool that can be used to numerically reproduce the projections presented in the Pew Research Center report “The Future of World Religions: Population Growth Projections, 2020-2070”, generate other projection variants based on the included input data, or create projections from user-supplied input data and adjustments to demographic and religious processes. This package may be most useful for users with training in demographic analysis and some experience using and programming in R. For inquiries, please contact: caspar@uek.krakow.pl.

Vignettes

The package ships four vignettes:

vignette("conducting-projections")

How to create a country list, assemble and run a projection, and export results to CSV using create_country_list, create_projection_object, variants_loader, and project.

vignette("visualising-projections")

How to save country-level and region-level plots using save_plots_all and save_plots_regions_all, and how to compare two scenarios side-by-side with save_plots_comparative_all.

vignette("exporting-results")

Column-by-column description of every CSV output file produced by save_csv_all, including example rows for the United States (ISO 840).

vignette("inner-workings")

Internal architecture: Country_object and Projection_object field reference, the Loader.R pipeline, and flow diagrams for the main projection procedure, migration loop, switching decomposition, and fertility factorisation.

Examples

# Quick one-step test projection (3 countries)
# Running a full projection is time-consuming.
# Wrapped in dontrun to avoid executing during documentation build.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
obj <- test_object_generator(object_name = "demo")
project(projection_object = obj, progress_bar = FALSE, save_totals = FALSE)
} # }
